items.title: The Neighbouring Hells' Four Gardens, and the Eight Cold Hells Begin

items.zh: 故此那落迦名為無間，多是造作無間之業來生是中。此但略說麁顯苦具，非於如是大那落迦中，所餘種種眾多苦具而不可得。
items.en: This is why this hell is called Uninterrupted — those reborn there have, for the most part, committed one of the acts of uninterrupted karma. This is only a brief account of the coarser, more evident instruments of suffering; it is not that the great hells contain no further, countless other instruments beyond these.

items.zh: 又於近邊諸那落迦中，有情之類受用如是治罰重苦。謂彼一切諸大那落迦皆有四方、四岸、四門，鐵牆圍遶。從其四方四門出已，其一一門外有四出園。謂煻煨齊膝。彼諸有情出求舍宅，遊行至此，下足之時、皮肉及血，並即消爛，舉足還生。次此煻煨無間，即有死屍糞泥。此諸有情為求舍宅，從彼出已，漸漸遊行，陷入其中，首足俱沒。又屍糞埿內多有諸蟲，名孃矩吒，穿皮入肉，斷筋破骨，取髓而食。次屍糞埿無間，有利刀劍仰刃為路。彼諸有情為求舍宅，從彼出已，遊行至此。下足之時，皮肉筋血悉皆消爛，舉足之時，還復如故。次刀劍刃路無間，有刃葉林。彼諸有情為求舍宅，從彼出已，往趣彼蔭，纔坐其下，微風遂起，刃葉墮落，斫截其身一切支節，便即躄地。有黑黧狗，摣掣脊𦛗而噉食之。從此刃葉林無間，有鐵設拉末梨林。彼諸有情為求舍宅，便來趣之，遂登其上。當登之時，一切刺鋒悉迴向下，欲下之時，一切刺鋒復迴向上。由此因緣，貫刺其身，遍諸支節。爾時便有鐵㭰大烏上彼頭上，或上其髆，探啄眼睛而噉食之。從鐵設拉末梨林無間，有廣大河，沸熱灰水彌滿其中。彼諸有情尋求舍宅，從彼出已，來墮此中。猶如以豆置之大鑊，然猛熾火而煎煮之，隨湯騰涌周旋迴復。於河兩岸有諸獄卒，手執杖索及以大網，行列而住，遮彼有情，不令得出，或以索羂，或以網漉。復置廣大熱鐵地上，仰彼有情而問之言：汝等今者欲何所須？如是答言：我等今者竟無覺知，然為種種飢苦所逼。時彼獄卒即以鐵鉗鉗口令開，便以極熱燒然鐵丸置其口中，餘如前說。若彼答言：我今唯為渴苦所逼。爾時獄卒便即洋銅以灌其口。由是因緣，長時受苦，乃至先世所造一切能感那落迦惡不善業未盡未出。此中若刀劍刃路、若刃葉林、若鐵設拉末梨林總之為一，故有四園。
items.en: Further, in the neighbouring hells, beings undergo grave punishment such as this: every great hell is surrounded by walls of iron, with four sides, four banks, and four gates; beyond each of the four gates lie four further gardens — knee-deep hot ash-embers, a swamp of corpses and filth crawling with flesh-eating worms, a road of upturned blades and a forest of blade-shaped leaves, and finally a vast river of scalding ash-water — each dissolving the flesh at every step, only for it to regenerate as quickly as it is destroyed, so the torment never actually ends.

items.zh: 又於寒那落迦受生有情，多受如是極重寒苦。謂皰那落迦中受生有情，即為彼地極重廣大寒觸所觸，一切身分悉皆卷縮，猶如瘡皰。故此那落迦名皰那落迦。皰裂那落迦與此差別。猶如皰潰，膿血流出，其瘡卷皺。故此那落迦名為皰裂。
items.en: Further, beings reborn in the cold hells, for the most part, undergo such extreme cold as this: those reborn in the Blistering Hell are touched by cold so vast and severe that the entire body curls inward, like a blister. This is why this hell is called Blistering. The Bursting-Blister Hell differs from this in that the blister has burst, pus and blood flowing out, the wound curling and wrinkling further still. This is why this hell is called Bursting-Blister.

items.title: The Remaining Cold Hells, and the Solitary Hell

items.zh: 又𠿒哳詀、郝郝凡、虎虎凡、此三那落迦由彼有情苦音差別以立其名。
items.en: Further, Chattering, Groaning, and Growling — these three hells are named for the distinct sounds of suffering their beings produce.

items.zh: 青蓮那落迦中，由彼地極重廣大寒觸所觸，一切身分悉皆青瘀，皮膚破裂，或五或六。故此那落迦名曰青蓮。紅蓮那落迦與此差別。過此青已，色變紅赤，皮膚分裂或十或多。故此那落迦名曰紅蓮。大紅蓮那落迦與此差別。謂彼身分極大紅赤，皮膚分裂或百或多。故此那落迦名大紅蓮。
items.en: In the Blue-Lotus Hell, beings are touched by cold so vast and severe that the entire body turns a bruised blue-black, the skin splitting into five or six parts. This is why this hell is called Blue Lotus. The Red-Lotus Hell differs from this: beyond the blue-black stage, the colour turns red, the skin splitting into ten parts or more. This is why this hell is called Red Lotus. The Great Red-Lotus Hell differs from this: the body turns an intense, deep red, the skin splitting into a hundred parts or more. This is why this hell is called Great Red Lotus.

items.zh: 又獨一那落迦中受生有情，各於自身自業所感，多受如是種種大苦。如吉祥問採菉豆子經中廣說。故此那落迦名為獨一。
items.en: Further, beings reborn in the solitary hells each undergo, through their own individual karma, a great variety of just such sufferings as these — as explained at length in the Sūtra of the Auspicious One's Question About Taking Up the Mung Bean. This is why this hell is called Solitary.

blocks.text: Today finishes the hells: the four "neighbouring" gardens outside each great hell, the eight cold hells, and the solitary hells found even in the human world. The cold hells are named for the sounds beings make, or for how their frozen skin splits, which our teachers explain in concrete detail.
Each great hot hell has four gates, and beyond each gate lie four "neighbouring" hells (近邊地獄), sometimes called gardens, which beings pass through after leaving the great hell:

items: **Knee-deep hot embers.** Master Cháng Bǎi: stepping in, skin, flesh, and blood dissolve; lifting the foot, they grow back.
**A swamp of corpses and filth**, full of worms that bore into the body.
**A road of blades**, a forest whose leaves are swords, and a forest of iron thorns.

blocks.text: The idea of passing through further suffering on the way out of hell expresses something the treatise says about karma generally: results do not stop abruptly when the main ripening is spent; residual results follow.
The cold hells lie in a different region. Their names describe the bodies or the cries of beings:

items: **Blistering** (皰): the whole body curls inward like a blister.
**Bursting Blister** (皰裂): the blister bursts and pus and blood flow.

**Chattering, Groaning, Growling** (喝哳詀、郝郝凡、虎虎凡), named for the sounds. Master Cháng Bǎi: in the first the lips are frozen and only the tongue moves; in the second the tongue is frozen and only the lips move; in the third neither moves and only a gasping sounds in the throat.
**Blue Lotus, Red Lotus, Great Red Lotus**: the skin turns blue or red and splits like petals, into five or six parts, ten or more, and a hundred or more.

blocks.text: The names are oddly beautiful for what they describe, which may be the point. The lotus, the very symbol of purity in Buddhism, becomes the image of a body split by cold.

Finally there are **solitary hells** (獨一地獄), scattered in the human world, by rivers, in mountains, in empty places. Day 23 noted that Mahāmaudgalyāyana reported seeing them. This brings the hells close: not only in a distant underworld but beside us.

The treatise has now described sixteen great hells, their neighbouring gardens, and the solitary hells. Its own conclusion, a few sections on (Day 29), is that in the hells "there is no pleasant feeling at all". The teachers' point throughout is that this account exists to support practice. In Venerable Miào Jìng's words from Day 4, what we do repeatedly now is what we will remember at the end; the hells are the far end of habits that begin as small moments of anger and cruelty.

quiz.q: The text says that beyond each great hell's four gates lie four gardens. According to Master Cháng Bǎi, what is the first garden beings meet on leaving the gate?
options: knee-deep hot ash-embers — stepping in, skin, flesh, and blood dissolve; lifting the foot, they regrow
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The first is the pain of knee-deep ash-embers — hot ash and fire as high as a person's knees … stepping in, skin, flesh, and blood all dissolve together, yet when the foot lifts they regrow." Next come the swamp of corpses and filth, the road of blades (with the blade-leaf and iron śālmali forests), and the vast river of ash. Beings leave "seeking shelter" — looking for rest — only to meet one garden worse than the last. (The Ru-Yi translation condenses the detailed passage into a single summary clause; logged in the correction list.)

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how do the Blistering and Bursting-Blister Hells differ?
options: in the first, the body curls into a blister; in the second, the blister has burst, pus and blood flow, and the wound wrinkles further
one is among humans, one underground
quiz.why: "The entire body curls inward, like a blister … The Bursting-Blister Hell differs from this in that the blister has burst, pus and blood flowing out, the wound curling and wrinkling further still." Both are cold hells, so A is wrong. Master Cháng Bǎi: the second is "more painful still."

quiz.q: Chattering, Groaning, and Growling are named for their sounds. According to Master Cháng Bǎi, how do the three differ?
options: Chattering: lips frozen, only the tongue moves; Groaning: tongue frozen, only the lips move; Growling: neither moves, only a gasping in the throat
the same sound at different volumes
they are the sound of wind
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Chattering: so cold the lips cannot move, only the tongue … Groaning: the tongue cannot move, only the lips … Growling: lips and tongue both frozen, only a quivering breath in the throat, a gasping sound." Each is colder than the last. Venerable Miào Jìng: the names come from "the distinct sounds of suffering their beings produce" — the sufferers' own voices, so C is wrong.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, into how many parts does the skin split in the Blue-Lotus, Red-Lotus, and Great Red-Lotus Hells?
options: five or six; ten or more; a hundred or more
quiz.why: Blue Lotus: "the skin splitting into five or six parts"; Red Lotus: "the colour turns red, the skin splitting into ten parts or more"; Great Red Lotus: "an intense, deep red, the skin splitting into a hundred parts or more." The body shifts from bruised blue to red to deep red, splitting ever finer like the petals of a lotus.
